title: README.dissector - some trivial edits
description:
Also undid a few done "don'ts" in dissectors, and thinking about
more checks that check_typeed_item_calls.py can do.

notes.body:
I was tempted to convert lots of calls of

col_add_fstr(...., "%s", val_to_str[_const](..))

to

col_add_str(...,       , val_to_str[_const](..))

but didn't, since the string is not really constant.  However, all of the matched strings are constant apart from the catch-all in the non-const case where the value will be substituted into the format string...  Parsing the format string "%s" is really quick, so won't make much of a difference.  Is it worth changing these too?
Don't do that. The pattern `printf("%s", string)` is used to prevent printf format evaluation of format characters in the input string.
Yes, but col_add_str() function doesn't check for format specifiers?  And it does take a deep copy of the string using ws_label_strcpy()

If the string part of the call is val_to_str_const(), then the string will be const (i.e., one of the value_string strings, or the "unknown" part.

If the string part is val_to_str(), there is a printf-style substitution for the "unknown (%d)" part, but whatever the result is will be copied anyway..
